summary: Deep technical session on model-specific runtime tuning for Llama, Mistral and Qwen; focus on MoE routing costs, RoPE scaling issues, KV cache/continuous batching and quantization tradeoffs. Customer wants predictable P95 latency and cost guidance for a Dedicated/Private deployment in VPC.
transcript:
[00:00] Maria Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll focus today on model-arch specific tuning - Llama, Mistral, Qwen and also ops implications for MoE and RoPE scaling. um Arjun will lead the bench parts.
[00:18] Daniel Park: Thanks, quick note - we've got a 95th percentile SLA target ~120ms for short chat flows, and cost needs to be within our committed budget, so both matter.
[00:33] Arjun Patel: Got it. We'll look at continuous batching + KV cache to keep p95 low. quick question - what kind of seq len are you seeing?
[00:42] Sana Iqbal: Mostly 64 tokens for prompts, but replies can be 100-400 tokens depending on user. we have a mix - embeddings + chat.
[00:50] Lexi Gomez: That distribution matters a lot for KV cache hit rate. With short prefixes you get much better amortization of attention.
[00:58] Markus Vogel: We're also evaluating MoE models for cost efficiency; heard mixed things about routing overhead. any data?
[01:06] Arjun Patel: yes early on MoE looks promising for FLOP/s cost, but routing can add memory-copy overhead and additional attention compute if more experts are activated. in practice routing costs are non-linear - if you go from 1 to 2 experts per token you see a step increase in latency.
[01:24] Maria Chen: Also worth noting our runtime supports sparse MoE routing optimizations, but the benefits depend on batch shape and hardware. on GPUs with PCIe hops the routing cost can be more visible.
[01:35] Daniel Park: We're planning Dedicated on 8xA100-ish nodes in our VPC. network latency between GPUs within node is ok. cross-node is a concern.
[01:44] Arjun Patel: For Dedicated, pinning experts to same node and keeping routing local helps. if routing triggers cross-node, latency spikes. our recommendation: benchmark with simulated routing patterns and limit experts per token to keep p95 targets.
[02:01] [00:02:01] Lexi Gomez: on RoPE scaling - Llama-style RoPE tends to degrade when you're extrapolating to much longer sequences; you can rescale or use ALiBi-like approaches, but that changes attention behavior. for inference we tune RoPE scaling factors and sometimes clamp rotary embeddings for long sequences to avoid drift.
[02:20] Sana Iqbal: Is that tuning per model or recorder-level parameter? we have mixed model families.
[02:26] Arjun Patel: It's often model-specific. Mistral's shorter-context models and Qwen's positional handling differ. Qwen sometimes uses a different positional scheme which is less sensitive, but performance/accuracy tradeoffs show up in long convo regen.
[02:40] Daniel Park: What about quantization? I know int8 can give huge perf wins but terp to quality?
[02:46] Maria Chen: Right - quantization profiles vary. we recommend post-training static quantization for many Llama variants and Mistral with per-channel scales; Qwen sometimes benefits from mixed precision (int8 for weights, float16 for critical layers). Redwood Optimize has recommended quant config per model and workload.
[03:04] Arjun Patel: Practically, int8 on FP16 hardware yields 1.8-2.4x throughput improvements, int4 can be 3-4x but with more quality risk. we run eval sets to measure degradation; often you can quantize the MLP weights heavily and keep attention weights higher precision.
[03:23] Lexi Gomez: Also watch KV cache memory layout - int8 KV cache reduces memory bandwidth and helps latency when cache fits L2/L3 better. if KV cache misses force recompute, p95 spikes.
[03:35] [00:03:35] Markus Vogel: How does continuous batching interact with SLA? we can't leak latency across requests.
[03:41] Arjun Patel: Redwood runtime uses latency budgets: short-tail requests can be served immediately while batching background work for throughput. there's a configurable max coalescing window - default 4-8ms - for low-latency workloads. you can tune for lower average cost by increasing window but p95 increases.
[03:57] Sana Iqbal: For our chat use case p95 requirement means we can't push large coalescing windows. what's recommended?
[04:03] Maria Chen: Start with 4ms and test. enable prefix KV caching and request-level routing to local experts. for your 64-token prompts and 100-400 replies, typical config: small batch window, KV cache enabled, quant int8 on non-critical layers. run benchmark to measure delta.
[04:19] Daniel Park: On VPC/on-prem: we need SOC2, SAML SSO and key management integration. do you support external KMS/HSM?
[04:27] Maria Chen: Yes for Private we integrate with customer KMS and HSM, and there are audit logs. we'll send the SOC2 docs.
[04:33] Arjun Patel: quick tunnel detail - if you're on-prem we can deploy a private control plane and data plane inside your VPC with peered monitoring endpoints; that avoids egress of sensitive tokens.
[04:44] [00:04:44] Lexi Gomez: Back to MoE - for routing costs we recommend two levers: limit top-k experts per token and use expert pruning for cold-start. also prefer hybrid MoE where routing is done at select layers not every layer to amortize routing overhead.
[05:00] Markus Vogel: That hybrid approach sounds reasonable; do you have numbers?
[05:05] Arjun Patel: On our internal tests, hybrid MoE (routing at every 4th transformer block) reduced routing overhead by ~30% while preserving most of the sparsity benefits - throughput improved vs full MoE and p95 reduced compared to routing every layer. exact numbers depend on hardware and kernel support.
[05:21] Daniel Park: Any model differences between Llama, Mistral, Qwen we should be aware of for inference tuning?
[05:28] Lexi Gomez: Llama-family often needs RoPE tuning for long sequences, Mistral has very compact MLP design which can compress well under quantization, Qwen has certain attention kernel differences and sometimes benefits from different KV cache tiling. memory access patterns change with each.
[05:46] Arjun Patel: also, Qwen's tokenizer and tokenization lengths affect batching efficiency - higher tokenization means more tokens per request which impacts throughput budgeting.
[05:55] Sana Iqbal: For the benchmarks we want: p95 latency on 64/128/256 token combos, throughput at 100qps and 1k qps, and cost per 1M tokens, both hosted and Dedicated. also MoE routing overhead breakdown.
[06:09] Maria Chen: We'll produce a benchmark plan and a spreadsheet - that'll include configs: model variant, quantization, batch window, KV cache enabled/disabled, experts per token, routing per-layer.
[06:18] [00:06:18] Arjun Patel: One gotcha: when you use KV cache across requests but have varying prompts, cache eviction patterns cause recompute. for high variability workloads we recommend segmented caching by user/session to improve hit rate.
[06:32] Markus Vogel: For privacy we need session isolation and no cross-tenant cache leakage. is that configurable?
[06:38] Maria Chen: yes per-tenant cache namespaces and eviction policies available; in Private you can enforce stricter rules.
[06:44] Lexi Gomez: Another detail - rope scaling: if you clamp rotary frequencies to avoid drift for very long sequences, you may slightly reduce short-context accuracy. it's a tradeoff. we'll test on your eval set.
[06:55] Sana Iqbal: What about the engineering effort for deployment on our infra? how long for a POC?
[07:00] Maria Chen: typical POC for Dedicated is 4-6 weeks: week 1 provisioning and security checks, week 2 basic integration and sample traffic, weeks 3-4 benchmarks and tuning. Private/on-prem can be a bit longer for network and KMS integration.
[07:12] Arjun Patel: for MoE experiments we recommend a short pilot with a small expert pool and a synthetic routing distribution similar to your traffic before scaling up.
[07:20] [00:07:20] Daniel Park: Any specific kernel or driver requirements we should pre-install?
[07:24] Arjun Patel: CUDA 12+, vendor driver recommended, and if using third-party quant libs we'll provide container images. for best performance install optimized NCCL and ensure GPU topology is correctly exposed.
[07:35] Maria Chen: ok let's recap next steps - Arjun you'll run a bench on the 8x nodes to validate p95 with KV cache and hybrid MoE, Maria will send docs and pricing, Sana gives prompt set. then follow-up review in two weeks.
[07:49] [00:07:49] Daniel Park: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:52] Maria Chen: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invite and the benchmark plan.
[07:56] [END]
